footer.tagline: Discover Nuwara Eliya like a local. Plan a trip that feels like yours.
footer.description: Curated journeys through misty tea country, high-elevation botanical trails and quiet colonial architecture in Sri Lanka’s historic hill station.

hero.tagline: Misty tea hills, colonial charm, and cool mountain air. Honest guidance from locals — completely free.

featuredExperiences.heading: Things worth doing here
featuredExperiences.subheading: Not a checklist. A considered set of ways to spend your time in the hill country.

items.title: Horton Plains & World's End
items.description: Walk the plateau at dawn and reach the escarpment edge where the land drops 880 metres into the valley below. Best in the dry season when the mist clears by mid-morning.
items.alt: Open plateau of Horton Plains at first light

items.title: Pedro Tea Estate
items.description: Follow the leaf from bush to cup inside one of the oldest working estates in the hill country. The factory tour is unhurried and the people who run it have been here for generations.
items.alt: Terraced tea rows on a hill-country estate

items.title: Gregory Lake at First Light
items.description: A quiet walk along the colonial-era bund before the town wakes. The lake sits perfectly still in the early morning, the surrounding hills reflected in it without distortion.
items.alt: Still lake surrounded by green hills at dawn

popularTripIdeas.heading: Trips that already make sense
popularTripIdeas.subheading: Whole itineraries, not a list of things to sort through yourself. Pick the one closest to your trip and adjust from there.

items.title: A Week in the Hills
items.description: The unhurried version. Enough time to actually settle into the pace of the hill country — tea estates in the morning, the plateau at dawn, long lunches, and evenings that end early because the air turns cold. Built for people who would rather do four things well than ten things quickly.
items.alt: Winding road through misty tea plantation hills

items.title: 3 Days as a Couple
items.description: A short, quiet trip built around slow mornings and one good view. Less itinerary, more mood.

items.title: The Long Weekend
items.description: For when you can only get away for two days but still want it to feel like a proper trip, not a rushed detour.
items.alt: Aerial view of rolling green hills under a cloudy sky

seasonalGuide.heading: Best Time to Visit
seasonalGuide.intro: Nuwara Eliya sits at 1,868m — it stays cool year-round, but the dry season (December to March) is when the hills are at their most magical.

seasons.title: The April Season
seasons.description: Nuwara Eliya at its fullest — horse racing, motor racing, and the town in bloom.

seasons.title: Dry Season
seasons.description: The clearest skies of the year. Best odds for uninterrupted views from Horton Plains.

seasons.title: Misty Mornings
seasons.description: Fog rolls through the tea hills before sunrise. Quieter, slower, and photogenic.

seasons.title: Shoulder Season
seasons.description: Fewer travelers, lower rates, and still good weather for getting around.

whyTrustUs.heading: Travel designed for the high country.
whyTrustUs.intro: Highland Sri Lanka rewards deliberate travelers who know when the mist falls and how mountain distances actually feel.

pillars.title: Elevation & Pacing
pillars.description: At nearly 1,900 meters, mountain roads turn 20 kilometers into a 60-minute journey. We structure schedules to protect you from car fatigue.

pillars.title: Microclimate Timing
pillars.description: Nuwara Eliya shifts from sparkling blue morning skies to drifting mist by early afternoon. We orient walks to catch panoramic views before the cloud rolls in.

pillars.title: Authentic Artisanry
pillars.description: Skip the souvenir-factory gift halls. We point you to working tea estates, gardens and heritage places run by people who know them well.

pillars.title: Curation Over Quantity
pillars.description: No generic lists of 100 roadside stalls. Every recommendation is handpicked, regularly reviewed, and matched to how you like to travel.

weather.title: The Weather Reality: Mist, Showers & Sunshine Windows
weather.description: Mornings are often bright, then cloud drifts in by midday and showers can follow in the afternoon. Do the important thing early and keep a waterproof layer in your bag.

transport.title: Getting Up the Hill: Train, Car or Bus
transport.description: The hill-country train is the scenic way up to Nanu Oya, a private car is the most flexible, and the public bus is the cheapest. Each suits a different kind of traveler.

seasons.title: Best Seasons: Horton Plains and the Dry Months
seasons.description: December to March is the most reliable window for clear mornings at World's End. April is the busiest month, and mid-year is quieter, wetter and very green.
